subject: Jairam Ramesh
guidance: Four career phases. Official roles, attributed arguments and bounded analysis remain distinct. Review counts describe registered fields, not historical completeness. All 40 era and ten gender dimensions have explicit dispositions.

rows.Finding / value: Jairam Ramesh (also styled Shri Jairam Ramesh), born 9 April 1954 in Chikmagalur, Karnataka; Indian National Congress politician, policy specialist and author.
B.Tech., M.S. and graduate study, at IIT Bombay, Carnegie Mellon University and MIT respectively. Graduate study is not presented as an MIT doctorate.
Fourth-term elected Rajya Sabha MP from Karnataka; present term began 1 July 2022. Congress general secretary responsible for communications, publicity and media, including digital media.
Technical and economic-policy assignments preceded Congress strategy, indirect parliamentary election and Union ministries. Influence rests substantially on policy expertise and party access.
Four confirmed Rajya Sabha elections: Andhra Pradesh in 2004 and 2010, Karnataka in 2016 and 2022. These are indirect state-representative elections; party campaign outcomes are separate.

Held junior Commerce and Power portfolios, independent charge of Environment and Forests, and cabinet responsibility for Rural Development with a period of additional Drinking Water and Sanitation charge.

The Bt-brinjal moratorium, Niyamgiri forest-clearance decision and NGT establishment made environmental regulation a prominent part of his record. POSCO shows that his approach also permitted conditional development.

Helped steer the 2013 land-acquisition legislation. Its consent, social-impact, compensation and rehabilitation framework is a documented institutional contribution; later distributional outcomes are less firmly established here.
Administered inherited rural programmes and women’s SHG credit expansion. NRLM launched on 3 June 2011, before his July appointment, so founding the mission is not credited to him.
Used parliamentary debate, committee scrutiny and litigation. He supported Aadhaar’s underlying idea while contesting its Money Bill route; review petitions were dismissed in 2021 with a dissent.

Communications appointment in June 2022 built on earlier strategy work. His yatra commentary connected party mobilisation to possible opposition cooperation, without proving a personal electoral effect.

Critics challenged the Bt-brinjal freeze, POSCO clearance and aspects of his public rhetoric. These policy and political disputes differ from the Doval defamation proceedings and the ECI request for evidence.
Apologised in December 2020. A January 2021 High Court order records his discharge on 19 December 2020 and transfer of the remaining case against other parties. This is not a conviction.

His publications combine insider policy documentation with historical biography, including Green Signals and A Chequered Brilliance. Author and publisher claims are distinguished from independent assessment.

Women’s SHGs and sanitation outreach had explicit gender relevance. Evidence of programme design and contemporary support is stronger than evidence of personal causal impact on women’s autonomy or safety.

The 2016 legislator vote count conflicts across reports; the official declaration confirms victory but not the count. Original 2004/2010/2022 detailed returns, policy outcomes and several gender mechanisms remain gaps.
Snapshot as of 16 November 2026. Four career phases, 40 era-context items and ten gender items. Source dates differ; historical findings are not live case-status certificates.
Findings and review status appear first. Expand grouped columns for dates, role, implementation and cautions. All citations opens each source; Claims and Evidence preserve passage-level checks.

Supported applies to the registered field, including explicit attribution or bounded analysis. It is not a completeness score. Unreviewed research limitations are not proof of absence. Blank counts mean unavailable or inapplicable, never zero.
Rajya Sabha ballots are cast by elected legislators. Popular-vote shares and single-opponent victory margins are not calculated. The reported 2022 count is a first-preference tally; 2016 is withheld.
